title: Conormal torsion for a one-dimensional completed component
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local domain, let $B=\widehat A$ be its maximal-ideal completion, and let $\mathfrak q$ be a minimal prime of $B$ with $\dim(B/\mathfrak q)=1$. There exist integers $n,c\ge1$ such that, for $J=\mathfrak q^n$, one has $JB_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $(\mathfrak mB)^c(J/J^2)=0$. Here $J/J^2$ is the quotient of the ideal $J$, viewed as a $B$-module, by its squared ideal. [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]

source.place: Tag 0AW3, lemma-not-formally-catenary, d=1 paragraph, with J a positive power of the minimal prime (not the kernel of localization).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $B=\widehat A$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB$. Thus every ideal of $B$ is finitely generated, by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. These facts apply because $A$ is Noetherian local and the completion is taken at its maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, d=1 paragraph; completion properties in Tags 0316, 05GI and 05GG

proof.text: Put $R=B_{\mathfrak q}$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-localization-radical] with the zero ideal of $B$: minimality of $\mathfrak q$ gives $\sqrt{(0)R}=\mathfrak qR$. The ideal $\mathfrak qR$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power], applied in $R$ to $I=\mathfrak qR$ and $K=0$, gives $n\ge1$ with $(\mathfrak qR)^n=0$. Set $J=\mathfrak q^n$. Then $JR=0$: each generator of the extended ideal $JR$ is a finite sum of coefficients times images of products of $n$ elements of $\mathfrak q$, and every such product belongs to $(\mathfrak qR)^n=0$. This establishes the first required assertion.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, d=1, nilpotence after localization; Tags 00FN and 00IM supply the explicit nilpotence argument

proof.text: Put $M=J/J^2$. It is finite: a finite set of ideal generators of $J$ maps to module generators of $M$. Also $JM=0$, since multiplying two elements of $J$ lands in $J^2$. If a prime $\mathfrak p$ does not contain $\mathfrak q$, choose $x\in\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$; then $x^n\in J$ annihilates $M$ and is invertible on $M_{\mathfrak p}$, so $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$. At $\mathfrak q$, each $y\in J$ has $y/1=0$ in $B_{\mathfrak q}$ by Step 2. The fraction definition of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $s\notin\mathfrak q$ with $sy=0$, so the class of $y$ also vanishes in $M_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $M_{\mathfrak q}=0$. Finally, if $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak n$, taking images in $B/\mathfrak q$ would give the prime chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak n/\mathfrak q$ of length two, contradicting $\dim(B/\mathfrak q)=1$ in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Every prime lies in $\mathfrak n$ since $B$ is local. These cases exhaust every prime other than $\mathfrak n$, hence $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subseteq\{\mathfrak n\}$.

source.place: Tag 0AW3, d=1, the omitted support calculation for the conormal module; support and fraction convention of Tag 00L2

proof.text: Let $H=\operatorname{Ann}_B(M)$. Finiteness of $M$ verified in Step 3 permits [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], which gives $V(H)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subseteq\{\mathfrak n\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], $\sqrt H$ is the intersection of all primes containing $H$. Every such prime equals $\mathfrak n$ by the preceding inclusion; therefore $\mathfrak n\subseteq\sqrt H$. If there are no such primes the intersection is the unit ideal, and the same inclusion holds. The ideal $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated since $B$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] in $B$ with $I=\mathfrak n$ and $K=H$ to obtain $c\ge1$ with $\mathfrak n^c\subseteq H$. By the definition of annihilator this is $\mathfrak n^cM=0$, namely $(\mathfrak mB)^c(J/J^2)=0$. Together with Step 2 this proves both clauses, including the case $J/J^2=0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q119-9d14ee44b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its four steps, all ten cited node statements, the only citer (Step 3 of lem-per-ratliff-formal-catenarity) and the Stacks more-algebra.tex Tag 0AW3 proof, including the d=1 paragraph, all check out. The statement is unchanged and matches what the parent uses. No new nodes and no SGA. Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian and lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring apply as stated, so B is Noetherian and local with maximal ideal mB. Step 2: B_q is Noetherian (lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian); lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-localization-radical with I=0 gives √0=qB_q; lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power with K=0 gives (qB_q)^n=0, so q^n B_q=0. Step 3, marked elementary, which I accept: each case is a short check from the localization fraction definition and the definition of Krull dimension. For p not containing q, a power x^n is a unit at p and kills M, so M_p=0. At q, the fraction criterion gives M_q=0. A prime strictly between q and n would give a chain of length 2 in B/q, against dim(B/q)=1. So Supp(M) is contained in {n}. Step 4: lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator, lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq and lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power give n^c ⊆ Ann(J/J^2); the case M=0 is covered. Small cases: a DVR (n=c=1); k[[x,y]]/(xy) with q=(x) (n=1); k[[t,e]]/(e^2) needs n=2. Accepted tool use: lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian, a generic Noetherianity tool that the unit has no replacement for. The grep over dag/nodes finds no duplicate: lem-per-conormal-torsion-algebraization and lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field are different statements. No fixes were needed.
